Theme

Body, health & movement

pace noun

of walking

also step, gait, at a quick pace, at a slow pace, keep pace with, quicken one’s pace

classical

Liv. 4.32.10: plēnō gradū, “at full pace” (Lewis & Short)
Phaedr. 2.7.6

gradus, gradūs m.

noun, fourth declension · Declension on Wiktionary

step, pace

With an adjective it gives the pace: plēnō gradū, citātō gradū (Liv. 28.14.17), quiētō et placidō gradū (Phaedr.); gradum addere, to quicken one’s pace (Liv. 26.9.5) (Lewis & Short). In the plural it is also the steps of a stair.

Other words

  • passus, passūs m. — a step, pace; the Roman pace of five feet

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 2.724: sequiturque patrem nōn passibus aequīs (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    The single stride, and as a measure the double step of five feet: mīlle passūs, a mile (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • comes quiētō sequitur et placidō gradū

    his companion follows at a quiet, steady pacePhaedr. 2.7.6

  • sequiturque patrem nōn passibus aequīs

    and he follows his father, not keeping pace with himVerg. A. 2.724 (Lewis & Short)

  • lentō gradū ambulāte, propter aestum sōlis

    walk slowly, because of the heat of the sunCord. Coll. 3.19

See also speed, step, walk.
